subject.title: [Feature Request] SKILL.md Instruction Isolation from Agent Context

question: What trusted/untrusted authority boundary should OpenClaw enforce for model-visible and explicitly invoked SKILL.md content?
rationale: This defines public security semantics across prompt precedence, role authority, memory influence, tool grants, sandbox/profile behavior, and upgrade compatibility, so automation cannot safely infer it from the current visibility-only implementation.

options.title: Design Boundary First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the capability schema, enforcement points, compatibility behavior, and regression-proof requirements before implementation.

options.title: Land Partial Mitigations Separately
options.body: Allow scanner, manifest-visibility, or deterministic-loading work to proceed as adjacent hardening while keeping this canonical isolation issue open until runtime enforcement exists.

options.title: Document Trusted Skills Assumption
options.body: Document that installed skills are trusted content and defer runtime isolation, explicitly accepting the residual security exposure for now.

recommendation.title: Design Boundary First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the capability schema, enforcement points, compatibility behavior, and regression-proof requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this issue as core security hardening and has history in the affected skill command policy.
